folders.title: Accessibility Infographics
folders.description: Infographics covering disabilities and health conditions.

folders.title: Highlights
folders.description: Posts and other resources that highlight topics and events related to neurodiversity and accessibility.

folders.title: Neurodiversity
folders.description: Highlights covering topics related to neurodiversity.

items.title: Neurodiversity Highlights
items.description: Every neurodiversity highlight in one file, each explaining a topic and how to support people, with useful links.

items.title: Body Doubling
items.description: Body doubling is working alongside someone else, to help you focus and get started on tasks.

items.title: Hidden Disabilities Sunflower
items.description: What the sunflower lanyard means, and how to support someone who wears one.

items.title: Infinity Symbol
items.description: The infinity symbol, which many neurodivergent people prefer to the puzzle piece, and what its colours mean.

items.title: Key Terminology
items.description: The difference between neurodiversity, neurodivergent, neurodiverse, neurotypical and neurotypes, and when to use each.

items.title: Masking
items.description: Masking is when neurodivergent people hide their natural traits to fit in, which can be exhausting.

items.title: Meetings
items.description: Why standard meetings can be hard for neurodivergent people, and simple changes that help.

items.title: Neurospicy
items.description: Why many people find the slang word 'neurospicy' a problem, and what to say instead.

items.title: Puzzle Piece Symbol
items.description: Why many autistic people find the puzzle piece symbol outdated or offensive.

items.title: Sensory Series: Light
items.description: How harsh lighting affects neurodivergent people, and how to make workspaces easier on the eyes.

items.title: Sensory Series: Sound
items.description: How everyday workplace noise can overwhelm neurodivergent people, and how colleagues can help.

items.title: Sensory Series: Touch
items.description: How textures, temperature and touch can affect neurodivergent people at work, and how to help.

items.title: Spiky Profiles
items.description: A spiky profile is being brilliant at some things but finding others very hard, which is common for neurodivergent people.

items.title: Spoon Theory
items.description: Spoon theory explains living with limited energy, and how to support colleagues who are 'low on spoons'.

items.title: Superpowers Debate
items.description: Why calling neurodivergence a 'superpower' can be tricky, and better ways to recognise strengths.

items.title: Tourette’s Syndrome
items.description: What Tourette's Syndrome is, beyond the myths, and how to be a good ally to someone with tics.

folders.title: Accessibility
folders.description: Highlights covering topics related to accessibility.

items.title: Accessibility Highlights
items.description: Every accessibility highlight in one file, each with what it’s for, how to support it and useful links, plus a glossary of terms.

items.title: Accessibility Debt
items.description: Accessibility debt is like technical debt, but for accessibility.

items.title: Accessibility Overlays
items.description: Accessibility overlays are automated tools that claim to find and fix accessibility issues on websites.

items.title: Accessibility Testing
items.description: Accessibility Testing is the process of checking a digital product to ensure it can be used by people with disabilities.

items.title: Accessible Authentication
items.description: When people can't use a login page, the harm can be serious.

items.title: Accessible Links
items.description: Link text should say where a link goes, so it makes sense on its own, including for people using assistive technology.

items.title: Accessible PDFs
items.description: We use PDF (Portable Document Format) to present all kinds of documents like guidelines, contractual agreements, data-heavy reports and even site maps.

items.title: Alt Text
items.description: Some people cannot see the images we display.

items.title: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA)
items.description: ARIA stands for 'Accessible Rich Internet Applications'.

items.title: ASCII Art
items.description: ASCII art is the practice of arranging punctuation and symbols to create a picture, like the ‘shrug’ ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ or drawings of animals.

items.title: Assistive Technology (Beyond Screen Readers)
items.description: Assistive Technology (AT) is any tool that helps people with disabilities use a computer.

items.title: Basic Accessibility Testing
items.description: Testing makes sure that what gets built actually works for everyone.

items.title: Breadcrumbs & Wayfinding
items.description: Breadcrumbs are a secondary navigation system that shows a user's current location within a site's hierarchy.

items.title: Buttons
items.description: Buttons let people take an action, such as submitting a form, saving information or opening a menu.

items.title: Captions & Transcripts
items.description: Captions are timed text that appears with a video to show spoken words, music, and sounds, helping viewers who are deaf or hard of hearing.

items.title: Carousels & Sliders
items.description: A carousel is a sliding banner that automatically cycles through images or messages on a webpage, like a digital billboard.

items.title: Colour-blind Series: Anomalous Trichromacy
items.description: Anomalous trichromacy is when all three types of colour sensing cells are present, but one doesn’t work as strongly as it should.

items.title: Colour-blind Series: Deuteranopia
items.description: Deuteranopia is a form of colour blindness that affects the ability to see green.

items.title: Colour-blind Series: Protanopia
items.description: Protanopia is a form of colour blindness that affects the ability to see red.

items.title: Colour-blind Series: The Rarer Types
items.description: Earlier entries in this series covered Protanopia, Deuteranopia, and Tritanopia.

items.title: Colour-blind Series: Tritanopia
items.description: Tritanopia is a form of colour blindness that affects the ability to see blue.

items.title: Colour Blindness
items.description: Colour blindness (or Colour Vision Deficiency) is about more than just seeing in black and white.

items.title: Colour Contrast
items.description: Websites, social media images, and out-of-home advertising should have a good colour contrast between text and background colour.

items.title: Consistency
items.description: Navigation, buttons and labels that look and work the same on every page help people find their way around.

items.title: Dark Mode
items.description: Dark mode is a colour option that flips the user’s view from the typical dark text on a light background to light text on a dark background.

items.title: Device Orientation
items.description: Websites and apps should work whichever way a screen is turned, as some people can’t turn their device.

items.title: Error Messages & Validation
items.description: Form errors are a major barrier for all users, but they can completely block users with disabilities.

items.title: Flashing & Photosensitivity
items.description: High-energy videos with strobing effects or rapid transitions can be physically dangerous.

items.title: Focus States
items.description: Focus states occur when an interactive element receives focus.

items.title: Focus Traps
items.description: A focus trap keeps keyboard focus inside one part of the page while it’s open, such as a modal, but always lets the user leave.

items.title: Fonts
items.description: Fonts are used everywhere, whether that's in a Word document, in a design, in a slide deck, or on a website.

items.title: Forms
items.description: An accessible form is an online form that everyone can fill in, including people with vision, movement, or cognitive disabilities.

items.title: Good Alt Text
items.description: While basic alt text just labels an image, good alt text explains its purpose.

items.title: Head Pointer
items.description: Head pointer allows users with limited hand function to control a computer cursor using head movements and, in some cases, facial expressions.

items.title: Headings
items.description: Most people are familiar with headings, whether that's a title in a document or a title sheet on a slide deck.

items.title: Hover states
items.description: Hover states are what happen when a mouse pointer moves over an interactive element.

items.title: Inclusive Language
items.description: Inclusive language means using words that respect everyone.

items.title: Keyboard Only
items.description: Keyboard only is a method for navigating the web using just a keyboard (not using the mouse at all).

items.title: Landmarks & Roles
items.description: Imagine trying to navigate a city with no street signs, where every building looks exactly the same.

items.title: Link Text
items.description: Many screen reader users navigate websites by pulling up a list of only the links on a page.

items.title: Meetings
items.description: Meetings are part of most workdays, and there are many ways to make them fully accessible and inclusive.

items.title: Modals
items.description: Modals are manually triggered pop-ups that provide extra information.

items.title: Neurodiversity & Inclusive Design
items.description: Neurodiversity describes the natural variations in how human brains function, process information, learn, and interact.

items.title: Personas
items.description: Personas are made-up people with real accessibility needs, which you can role-play as while testing your work.

items.title: Prefers-reduced-motion
items.description: Some people struggle with motion on websites.

items.title: Presentations
items.description: Most people will have to give a presentation at some point.

items.title: QR Codes
items.description: A QR (Quick Response) code is a type of two-dimensional barcode.

items.title: Screen reader only styling
items.description: Screen reader only styling ensures that everyone who uses a website can access the important information it contains.

items.title: Screen Readers
items.description: Screen readers are pieces of software that announce content audibly.

items.title: Shifting Left
items.description: Imagine baking a cake, pulling it out of the oven, and realising you forgot the sugar.

items.title: Social Media: Alt Text
items.description: On social media, images often hold the core message or punchline.

items.title: Social Media: Custom Fonts
items.description: People often use generator websites to make their text look unique (e.g.

items.title: Social Media: Emojis
items.description: Emojis add personality and tone to messages, but for a screen reader user, they are read aloud as literal text descriptions.

items.title: Social Media: Hashtags
items.description: Imagine trying to read a sentence where all the spaces have been removed.

items.title: Tap Targets
items.description: Buttons and links should be big enough, with enough space around them, to press without hitting something else by mistake.

items.title: Temporary & Situational Disabilities
items.description: People often link accessibility with permanent disabilities.

items.title: Text Alternatives for Complex Images
items.description: Standard 'alt text' is great for simple photos, but it often fails for complex data like charts, graphs, flowcharts, or infographics.

items.title: Time Limits
items.description: Time limits refer to when a page sets a time limit on doing a certain action.

items.title: Tooltips & Popovers
items.description: Tooltips and popovers give users extra info on demand (like for an icon button).

items.title: Touch Gestures
items.description: Imagine trying to open a heavy door, but the rule is you can only use your pinky fingers.

items.title: Zooming
items.description: Some people need to make the text and images on a website bigger to see them clearly.

items.title: Accessible Meeting Checklist
items.description: A checklist of things to ensure meetings are accessible to all attendees.

items.title: Email Signature Additions
items.description: Some template examples that can be added to an email signature to share information about accessibility, neurodiversity, and working differences.

items.title: Meeting Invite Template
items.description: A meeting invite template, created so that no information gets missed when setting up meetings.
